title: How we built Polluxkart
excerpt: A teardown of the commerce stack we shipped for Polluxkart — architecture choices, trade-offs, and what we would redo.
content:
# How we built Polluxkart

Polluxkart needed a storefront and ops tooling that could keep pace with a growing Indian commerce brand — without drowning the team in platform lock-in.

## What we shipped

- Custom storefront UX tuned for mobile-first traffic
- Ops tooling for catalog and order workflows
- Incremental deploys so marketing could ship without waiting for a "big bang" release

## Architecture trade-offs

We favoured boring, observable services over novelty. Checkout latency and inventory correctness beat clever abstractions.

## Metrics that mattered

Continuous improvements on the live storefront at [polluxkart.com](https://polluxkart.com), with ops visibility that the team could actually run day-to-day.

## What we would redo

Instrument conversion funnels earlier. Content and case studies convert better when metrics are measured from week one.
author: Softogram Team

title: What custom software really costs in India (2026)
excerpt: Honest ranges for MVPs, SaaS builds, and enterprise integrations — and the line items buyers forget to budget.
content:
# What custom software really costs in India (2026)

Buyers keep asking for one number. Reality is a range driven by scope, integrations, compliance, and how many unknowns you still have.

## Typical engagement bands

- **Landing / brochure site:** scoped content + contact — measured in weeks, not months
- **MVP web app:** auth, core workflow, basic admin — often 8–16 weeks depending on integrations
- **SaaS / multi-tenant:** identity, billing, observability — plan for backlog beyond v1

## Hidden line items

Discovery workshops, UAT cycles, third-party API limits, KYC/PCI if you touch payments, and post-launch support.

## How Softogram quotes

We start with a written proposal: scope, assumptions, milestones, and what is explicitly out of scope. Fixed-ish milestones beat endless hourly fog — with change orders when scope expands.

title: Website vs web app: which does your business need?
excerpt: A practical decision guide for founders choosing between a marketing site, a web app, or a hybrid.
content:
# Website vs web app: which does your business need?

If visitors mainly read and inquire, you need a **website**. If users log in and do work, you need a **web app**.

## Website signals

- Marketing pages, services, blog, contact
- SEO and brand narrative matter more than complex state
- Updates are content-driven

## Web app signals

- Accounts, roles, dashboards, workflows
- Data integrity and permissions matter
- You will ship repeatedly after launch

## Hybrid is common

Many Softogram clients start with a sharp marketing site + a thin authenticated area for clients/docs — then grow the product surface as usage proves demand.

title: Launch checklist: 25 things before going live
excerpt: A practical pre-launch checklist covering security, SEO, ops, and conversion — use it as a free lead magnet or an internal gate.
content:
# Launch checklist: 25 things before going live

Use this as a gate before production traffic.

## Security & trust
1. TLS valid on apex + API hosts
2. Security headers (HSTS, nosniff, frame denial)
3. Contact rate limits + honeypot
4. Secrets not in the frontend bundle
5. Dependency audit on the API

## Reliability
6. Uptime monitor on site + API
7. TLS expiry alerts
8. Error logging with alerts
9. Database / file backup story
10. Rollback plan for the last deploy

## Product quality
11. Mobile pass on core flows
12. Empty / error / loading states
13. Form validation + success UX
14. Analytics events after consent
15. Accessible focus states on CTAs

## SEO & content
16. Unique title + description per route
17. OG image that is not a broken URL
18. Sitemap submitted to Search Console
19. JSON-LD for Organization / BlogPosting
20. 404 page that routes people home

## Conversion
21. Working WhatsApp / phone with country code
22. Booking CTA to a real calendar
23. Support email on your domain
24. One case study with real metrics
25. Post-launch ownership (who watches inbox?)

Ship when the checklist is boring — not when the homepage looks exciting.
author: Softogram Team
